subject: gk
question: Which ports belong to the western coast of India?

options.text: Kandla port, Mormugao port, Kolkata port
Kandla port, Mormugao port, Kochi port
Kandla port, Mormugao port, Chennai port
Kandla port, Haldia port, Kochi port

solution:
The correct answer is __**Kandla port, Mormugao port, Kochi port**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kandla port, Mormugao port, Kochi ports **belong to the western coast of India.
 
• **Kandla Port:**
 
 
• Located in the Kutch district of Gujarat, Kandla port is one of the largest ports in India and plays a crucial role in the country's trade activities.
 
• It serves as a major hub for exporting various goods, including petroleum products, grains, salt, and textiles.
 
• Kandla port is strategically positioned near the Gulf of Kutch, offering easy access to international shipping routes.
 
 
 
• **Mormugao Port:**
 
 
• Situated in Mormugao, Goa, Mormugao port is another significant port on the western coast of India.
 
• It primarily handles the export of iron ore, manganese ore, and other minerals mined in the region.
 
• Mormugao port is known for its natural harbor, which allows for the smooth movement of large cargo ships.
 
 
 
• **Kochi Port:**
 
 
• Kochi port, located in the city of Kochi (formerly Cochin) in Kerala, is a major maritime gateway on the western coast.
 
• It is one of the oldest ports in India and serves as a key center for international trade, particularly in the southern region.
 
• Kochi port handles a diverse range of cargo, including spices, seafood, coir, and containerized goods.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The** western coastal plains of India** extend from **Kerala in the south to Gujarat in the north, traversing through the states of Karnataka, Goa, and Maharashtra.**
 
• Stretching approximately **1,500 kilometers** in length and measuring between 10 to 25 kilometers in width, these plains are a significant geographical feature of the region.
 
• The western coastal plains are characterized by their division into three distinct parts: the Canara coast, the Konkan coast, and the Malabar coast.
 
• Each of these regions has its own unique topographical and cultural attributes.
